Action Plan:
1. Arrange comprehensive blood tests (FBC, U&E, LFT, TFT, vitamin B12/folate, ferritin) to investigate fatigue, weight loss, nausea, and palpitations.
2. Patient to telephone Babylon support (number in app) today to book the blood draw; clinician will submit electronic request form.
3. Review results promptly; schedule follow-up appointment once results available to decide on management (including possible re-initiation of levothyroxine).
4. Safety-net advice given: attend ED immediately for new-onset chest pain, persistent vomiting, or altered bowel habit; re-contact service if symptoms worsen.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for consult: 3-month history of low mood, fatigue, loss of appetite; 6-month unintentional weight loss (~1 stone).  
• Other symptoms: episodic palpitations/subjective shortness of breath in lifts; intermittent nausea; no vomiting, no diarrhoea, no blood or mucus in stool; no chest pain.  
• Onset/progression: appetite loss began ≈3.5 months ago after job change; weight loss preceded this by several months.  
• Past medical history: Underactive thyroid.  
• Medications: Levothyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented) – patient stopped “since changing doctor.”  
• Allergies: not discussed.  
• Social: 35-year-old male lawyer; married; no other social factors noted.

Objective:
• No physical examination performed during teleconsultation.  
• No vital signs available.  
Investigations ordered: Comprehensive blood panel as above.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Fatigue, anorexia, weight loss
   - Assessment: Constitutional symptoms – cause undifferentiated (anaemia, hypothyroidism recurrence, mood disorder, systemic illness).
   - Differential: Hypothyroidism, depression, iron-deficiency anaemia, chronic infection, malignancy (less likely).
   - Investigations: FBC, U&E, LFT, TFT, B12/folate, ferritin.
   - Treatment: To be guided by results; follow-up arranged.

2. Palpitations / episodic shortness of breath
   - Assessment: Possible anxiety-related palpitations vs metabolic (thyroid, anaemia).
   - Differential: Anxiety/panic, thyrotoxicosis, arrhythmia, anaemia.
   - Investigations: Included in blood panel; consider ECG if symptoms persist or worsen.
   - Treatment: Safety-net advice re chest pain; revisit after bloods.

3. Known hypothyroidism – medication non-adherence
   - Assessment: Likely uncontrolled hypothyroidism due to cessation of levothyroxine.
   - Investigations: TFT within blood panel.
   - Treatment: Reinstate / titrate levothyroxine once TFT results reviewed.
   - Referral: Endocrinology only if difficulty achieving control.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Allergies not elicited; current medication list may be incomplete (needs reconciliation); no mental-health screening questions used.  
● Internal conflicts: Duration of weight loss (patient unsure; “started earlier,” “six months”) – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor conversational overlaps, no significant inaudible sections.
